items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Abby Mitchell was a great star in those days... Every show, she was quitting.

ctx.x: Was this show called the Chocolate Kitties, or what was it called?

No, it was the Club Alabam's show. Just like The Cotton Club's show, it was called the Club Alabam's show. But this was a great show. And I learnt one thing, because Abby Mitchell was a great star in those days, you see. She could sing very well. Will Marion Cook used to come there because that was his wife and set down there. And a lot of others used to come there during the rehearsal days. And I could then pick up the tempo, but I didn't know how to retard the tempo along with the singer. So I just wasn't…

tape anytime. When I got the chance to go to Europe -- I'm a little ahead of my story, but I'll come back. When I got a chance to go to Europe, there was a great man -- which I considered a great man. Rosamund Johnson, a great Negro composer and a student of music, see. And he's written a lot of spirituals, I mean he's edited a lot of spirituals and had some folk songs of his own, I mean, art songs of his own.
